subject.title: Add an FxTwitter read transport for public lookups, threads, profiles, and search

question: Should Birdclaw adopt FxTwitter as a supported opt-in public-read provider, and if so should the first release permit arbitrary self-hosted base URLs or only a narrowly validated endpoint policy?
rationale: The codebase can accommodate another adapter, but neither source nor vision decides whether Birdclaw should assume ongoing ownership of this third-party provider, its privacy disclosure, and its configurable outbound-network boundary.

options.title: Approve a staged provider
options.body: Start with explicit post, thread, profile, public-timeline, and search reads through existing canonical interfaces, with strict capability errors and a narrowly defined HTTPS endpoint policy.

options.title: Approve hosted endpoint only
options.body: Support the documented public FxTwitter service first and defer arbitrary self-hosted endpoints until redirect, DNS, and private-network rules are designed and tested.

options.title: Decline provider ownership
options.body: Keep Birdclaw focused on its existing authenticated transports and leave FxTwitter integration outside the supported product surface.

recommendation.title: Approve a staged provider
recommendation.body: Start with explicit post, thread, profile, public-timeline, and search reads through existing canonical interfaces, with strict capability errors and a narrowly defined HTTPS endpoint policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner controls the vision-level decision to add and support another live provider and configuration surface.
